verdict_label: Some flexibility, but be on time
explanation: Punctuality is valued in Indian business culture, but meetings don't always start exactly on time, and some scholars classify South Asian business culture as relatively polychronic (more flexible about schedules), though that broad regional label is itself debated. International visitors are still expected to arrive on schedule themselves as a sign of professionalism, and turning up late without notice to a meeting with senior leaders or external clients can read as disrespectful.
local_tip: Arrive on time yourself even if your Indian counterparts run a little late, and send a quick message if you expect to be delayed.

also_check.note: Punctuality is critical; arriving even a few minutes late is considered disrespectful.
Arriving 15-30 minutes late to social and some business meetings is common and generally accepted.
Punctuality is seen as a sign of professionalism; lateness is viewed as unreliable.
